December, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:37901
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Himanshu Joshi

On The 29th Of December, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 60186 of 2025
 Mahesh Kumar Jain
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Garvit Singh - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Rahul Solanki - Govt. Advocate for the responden

Order 
This first application has been filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 550/2025, registered at Police Station - Rajgarh District Rajgarh (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC and Section(s) 7A, 8, 11, 12(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act and Section(s) 66D and 72 of IT Act.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 7.6.2025.
Heard the arguments.
Perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application, case diary and the relevant material on record.

Learned counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the applicant is falsely implicated in the alleged offence for the reason that he was working as an Accountant in the Civil Hospital, Rajgarh.
Applicant was not aware of the forgery, cheating NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:37901 2 MCRC-60186-2025 and misappropriation committed by other accused.
He has merely forwarded the bills submitted by the Outsourcing Agency for payment to higher authorities.
The applicant is implicated on the basis of information given by the co-accused in police custody.
No incriminating material showing complicity of the applicant in the embezzlement was recovered and seized in the investigation.
Learned counsel further referring to the FIR at Crime No. 318/2025 submits that the applicant was implicated on identical allegations for the period between 2022-2025.
The applicant was extended benefit of bail v i d e order dated 22.07.2025 by the trial Court.

Thereafter, present prosecution at Crime No.
550/2025 was initiated on identical allegations for previous period i.e. between 2016-2022.

sentences.text: Court had considered the allegations against the applicant for previous period also while granting bail.
No new material was seized at the instance of the applicant in the present prosecution.
Rather, the Investigation Officer has relied on seizure memo of previous prosecution in Crime No.318/2025.
The applicant is not maker of forged bills.

The prosecution for offence punishable under the Prevention of Corruption Act is not sustainable, as the permission to investigate under Section 17-A of the Act was not taken from the competent authority.
The alleged offence is not made out against the applicant.
Investigation is almost complete.
Further custodial interrogation of the applicant is not needed in the matter.
There is no likelihood of tampering with evidence by the applicant.
Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the aged applicant and his family members.
Co-accused Ramdayal alias Sonu has been extended benefit of bail by this Court vide order dated 27.09.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:37901 3 MCRC-60186-2025 42032/2025.
Applicant is ready to cooperate in the further investigation/trial.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Learned counsel refers to 05 criminal antecedent of the applicant, as mentioned in the case diary.
In reply, learned counsel for the applicant submits that similar prosecution was earlier registered at Crime No. 318/2025, wherein applicant was extended benefit of bail by the trial Court.
The same is pending for trial now.
Applicant has never been convicted for any offence.

According to the material available on case diary, Civil Hospital, Rajgarh has outsourced the job of supply of sweepers/sanitation workers to M/s Pratham National Security Company, Indore in the year 2016, which was extended in the year 2024.
Kuldeep Mishra, Proprietor of M/s Pratham National Security Company, Indore gave petty contract to Rajesh Khare.

Rajesh Khare in association with Sanjeev Sharma(applicant), Steward of Civil Hospital, Rajgarh and Ramdayal @ Sonu,
Computer Operator at Civil Hospital, Rajgarh
had manipulated and submitted forged Bio-metric attendance sheets and misappropriated the public money by submitting forged bills.
The amount was paid into the account of Service Provider M/s Pratham National Security Company, Indore.

The Police Station Rajgarh registered FIR for offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of IPC and Section(s) 7A, 8, 11, 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act and Section(s) 66D and 72 of IT Act against Rajesh Khare and Kuldeep Mishra, Krishna Kumar Tiwari, Mahesh Jain and Sanjeev NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:37901 4 MCRC-60186-2025 Sharma (applicant).
Accordingly, applicant - Sanjeev Sharma was apprehended on 08.09.2025.
He is in custody ever since.
The forged Bio- metric attendance sheets were recovered and seized.

Initially,
the FIR at Crime No. 318/2025 was registered.

The main beneficiary of the transactions Kuldeep Mishra and Krishna Kumar, the Proprietor and Manager of M/s Pratham National Security Company, Indore respectively and the Accountant Mahesh i.e. the present applicant were extended benefit of bail by the trial Court.
Later, the present prosecution was initiated on identical allegations for the preceding period between 2016-2022.
There is no allegation of misuse of liberty against applicant.
Prima facie, he is not the maker of forged bills or the direct beneficiary of transaction.
The investigation is almost complete.

sentences.text: The veracity of prosecution, role and complicity of the applicant will be determined after evidence in the trial.
As informed, the applicant is aged around 37 years.
He is working as Accountant in the Pratham National Security Company, Indore and has the responsibility of dependent family.
Considering these aspects, there appears to be no possibility of fleeing from justice.

In absence of any substantial criminal past and previous conviction for any major offence, considering the socio-economic status of the applicant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with evidence or influencing the witnesses by the applicant.
There appears to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of the applicant.
However, the observations, herein-above, are recorded for present application only.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:37901 5 MCRC-60186-2025

Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the case, in the light of aforestated facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant - Mahesh Kumar Jain shall be released on bail in connection with Crime, as mentioned in first paragraph of this order, upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh only) with one surety of the same amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for compliance with the following conditions :
(For convenience of understanding by accused and surety, the conditions of bail are also reproduced in Hindi as under):-
(1) Applicant shall remain present on every date of hearing as may be directed by the concerned court; (1) 
  

  
 

   




 



     
        

  (2) Applicant shall not commit or get involved in any offence of similar nature; (2)

(3) Applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement,
threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them/him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to the police officer;
(3)
